The main takeaway from our work is that
the condylar height is of less clinical significance than previously thought.
the reestablishment of the occlusion and function does not occur as a result of the anatomic restitution of the condylar height but rather as a result of muscle adaptation.
the condyle can be displaced and dislocated without causing pain or loss of function, and that the condyle does not necessarily have to be reduced to restore function and occlusion.
